title: Staff Tech Lead, Web & Developer Products
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>Our everyday digital experiences are in the middle of a realtime revolution: chatting alongside a livestream, getting realtime financial updates, or working with colleagues in a shared online space. Consumers now expect realtime as standard, and Ably powers a large part of it.</p> <p>We put developers first. Our products help teams build, extend, and deliver realtime digital experiences, delivering over 700 billion messages to more than 2 billion devices every month. Teams at HubSpot, Fin, Dialpad, NASCAR, Sportsbet, and General Motors all build on Ably.</p> <p>Working at Ably means helping build the infrastructure that will shape the next generation of the internet. More of what people do online is becoming live, shared and interactive, which only makes what we build more relevant and more necessary. AI is the latest place that shows up. There's still so much to build, and we'd like your help with it.</p></div><h2><strong>About this role</strong></h2> <p>As the Staff Tech Lead for the Developer Experience team at Ably, you’ll report directly to our CTO and co-own the DevEx vision and strategy. You’ll lead the engineering team that owns our customer-facing web platform - our dashboard, documentation platform, and control plane - transforming it into a world-class experience for our users.</p> <p>You are a senior, hands-on engineer who’s passionate about building for developers like yourself; someone who’ll obsess over the developer journey and elevate the user experience of the Ably platform. You’ll blend deep full-stack expertise with a strong product mindset, and lead a team of engineers working on initiatives where the feedback loop is immediate, because you and your team are the target users of the very ecosystem you are building.</p> <p>Ably is an AI-forward organisation and this is a leadership role for an AI-first engineer. You must have confident, hands-on experience of AI-assisted development and be able to define how a team actually works with these tools day to day, and tell the difference between genuine leverage and noise.</p> <h2><strong>Day to day you will</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Obsess over developer experience. </strong>You’ll have broad responsibility for elevating how developers interact with Ably’s platform and services, partnering with the DevEx PM as a unified leadership team to deliver a developer experience that becomes a reference point for the industry.</li> <li><strong>Define and lead on AI-first working practices.</strong> You’ll be the catalyst and standard-setter for AI-enabled development across the team. You’ll leverage LLMs and AI tools to accelerate velocity, design workflows, set the guardrails and coach engineers to use them well - without compromising on engineering integrity.</li> <li><strong>Lead technical execution and vision.</strong> You’ll lead a team of five engineers building customer-facing web applications and own the technical architecture and design decisions for our dashboard, docs platform, marketing website, and billing UI.</li> <li><strong>Drive a product-first engineering culture.</strong> You’ll foster an environment where engineers are themselves principal stakeholders of product features, and obsess over customer outcomes. You’ll challenge the "feature factory" mentality and build a team that takes true ownership of the product.</li> <li><strong>Thrive in a rapid iteration environment.</strong> You’ll operate in a high-velocity workspace where PMs, customers, and engineers co-create features. You’ll lead the team in working full-stack to iterate, improve, and ship improvements quickly.</li> <li><strong>Guide engineering outcomes and quality.</strong> You’ll set and enforce high standards for code review, testing, and production readiness. You will participate in incident response and coordinate with the Infrastructure team on platform dependencies and deployments.</li> <li><strong>Mentor and grow the team.</strong> You’ll manage performance, career development, and hiring. You will hold the team accountable for delivery commitments while providing the mentorship needed to turn engineers into product-minded leaders.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>We'd love to talk if you have</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Real, demonstrable experience leading AI-first engineering. You champion the use of AI as a productivity multiplier for the team, and have led a team that ships with LLMs and AI tooling embedded in its daily workflow. You see AI as an enabler for higher velocity and output, not a replacement for engineering judgment, and hold strong, evidence-based views on what works and what doesn’t.</li> <li>Extensive experience leading technical teams in technical B2B SaaS or API-first products, with a track record of product-minded engineering teams that take initiative and ownership of product outcomes.</li> <li>A strong software engineering background with genuine full-stack fluency. You must have enough depth across the web stack to credibly lead and challenge senior web engineers. Hands-on experience with React and TypeScript is valuable, but sound engineering judgement and technical gravitas matter more than specific frameworks.</li> <li>You have a natural empathy and strong instincts for what developer customers want because you are the target user. You are genuinely excited about building developer tools and can tap into immediate feedback loops. You understand API design, documentation, and the nuances that differentiate a great developer journey.</li> <li>Experience at a startup or growth-stage company or adaptability to thrive in a fast-paced, agile environment with a focus on rapid iteration. To be effective in this role you’ll need excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Bonus points if you have</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Deep production experience building and shipping customer-facing web applications at scale with React and TypeScript.</li> <li>Experience delivering solutions used by software developers (developer tooling or APIs) or similar technical personas.</li> <li>An understanding of pub/sub and familiarity with distributed systems and event based architectures.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><h2><strong>What’s it like to work at Ably?</strong></h2> <p>You'll join a team of around 60 people, working directly alongside senior engineering and leadership. No layers, no bureaucracy, and real ownership from day one.</p> <h3>Remote-first</h3> <p>We hire the best people wherever they are across the UK and Europe, trust them to own their work, and share decisions and feedback openly. Twice a year, in February and August, we all meet in person, and we expect everyone to be there.</p> <p>Remote-first comes with trade-offs. On one side: flexibility, no commute, long stretches of focus time, and a wider pool of people to hire from. At its core, this is an AI-focussed role; you’ll be in charge of  setting up the foundations that empower engineers to produce first-class developer documentation with AI at scale. You’ll use AI to automate checks, maintain quality, and allow for rapid iteration in the content itself, as well as in the documentation platform. You’ll still be setting the standards for technical content across the business, and using your expertise to shape the information architecture.</p> <p>This is a modern take on technical writing; you’ll be using AI to both increase your own output, whilst also increasing the velocity of other contributors. The same core values still apply though - ensuring that users can quickly understand and succeed with Ably.</p> <h2><strong>Day to day you will</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Use AI to produce quality content. </strong>You’ll write reusable prompts and skills that docs contributors can use to ensure their content meets Ably’s quality standards. </li> <li><strong>Define and uphold content standards</strong>. You'll help define what great looks like; from docs structure and style to making sure that PRs are always exceeding standards. You’ll leverage AI to check for technical accuracy, and make sure that content always assists developers in learning and succeeding with Ably in the fastest and easiest ways possible.</li> <li><strong>Build engaging educational content templates. </strong>You’ll lead by example by producing reference content that others can use as a pattern to write similar content. This will be in the format of templates and skills that team members can leverage.</li> <li><strong>Empower engineers to write great content</strong>. You'll coach and support engineering contributors to ensure that they’re always producing accurate, well-structured, developer-friendly content.</li> <li><strong>Champion effective AI use</strong>. You'll promote the use of AI for efficiency, while maintaining a sharp eye for quality ensuring content meets editorial standards, is technically accurate, and is free from AI-generated patterns that undermine trust or clarity.</li> <li><strong>Maintain and elevate the docs platform</strong>. You'll take responsibility for shaping the documentation platform's components, structure and tooling. This includes making sure content is logically structured, and easily navigable, and that it helps external developers understand Ably in new and exciting ways. </li> </ul> <h2><strong>We'd love to talk if you have</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Proven success creating technical content for developers, such as documentation, API references and guides; with a portfolio that others have visibly learned from.</li> <li>Experience reviewing and giving feedback on technical writing, with the ability to coach others to improve their craft.</li> <li>Experience and a desire to work in an AI-forward environment. Experience in automation, working with agents and producing quality content at scale is a bonus.</li> <li>Experience of using AI tools as a core part of your workflow for writing, research and coding, as well as understanding their output and limitations.</li> <li>Familiarity with APIs, SDKs, and modern web development tools, with the ability to read, write and reason about code examples in at least one programming language (ideally JavaScript).</li> <li>Strong instincts for developer experience, particularly around onboarding, and a genuine desire to produce experiences that delight developers.</li> <li>A proactive, self-directed mindset with the ability to take ownership of projects end to end, from ideation through to completion.</li> <li>Experience at a startup or growth-stage company, or the adaptability to thrive in a fast-paced, agile environment with a focus on rapid iteration, with excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Bonus points if you have</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience in maintaining and shaping a documentation platform or developer portal.</li> <li>Familiarity with information architecture principles and content strategy.</li> <li>Familiarity with git-driven workflows for managing content changes.</li> <li>Some knowledge or understanding of event-driven architecture.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><h2><strong>What’s it like to work at Ably?</strong></h2> <p>You'll join a team of around 60 people, working directly alongside senior engineering and leadership. No layers, no bureaucracy, and real ownership from day one.</p> <h3>Remote-first</h3> <p>We hire the best people wherever they are across the UK and Europe, trust them to own their work, and share decisions and feedback openly. Twice a year, in February and August, we all meet in person, and we expect everyone to be there.</p> <p>Remote-first comes with trade-offs. On one side: flexibility, no commute, long stretches of focus time, and a wider pool of people to hire from. On the other: it can feel isolating, relationships take effort to build, and you miss the chance conversations an office creates. As our only recruiter, you'll need to manage your own time and stay close to the hiring managers and candidates you work with.</p> <p>If you do your best work with trust and autonomy, this will suit you. If you'd rather have an office around you every day, it probably isn't the right fit.</p> <p>Our six values shape how we work day to day:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Open for all.</strong> We default to sharing openly: source, decisions, and feedback, with open minds to match.</li> <li><strong>Tech needs humanity.</strong> We build with empathy, for colleagues and developers alike.</li> <li><strong>Even the best do better.</strong> We keep raising our own bar, driven by curiosity, not complacency.</li> <li><strong>Bias for action.</strong> Once we know enough to act, we act, rather than waiting for certainty.</li> <li><strong>Dependable by default.</strong> We take real ownership of what we ship and what we promise.</li> <li><strong>Bold creativity wins.</strong> We treat big constraints as a reason to think differently, not less.</li> </ul> <p>You can read more about how we defined these values on <a href="ably.com/blog/ably-values">our blog</a>, and see the team behind them on our <a href="ably.com/careers">careers page</a>.</p> <h2>Diversity, inclusion, and belonging at Ably</h2> <p>We believe our differences as individuals are what make us great. With a global presence in over 30 countries, we're here to bring some excitement to the leisure and attractions industry and make a difference! Our mission is to help businesses operate smoothly and create fun and memorable guest experiences by providing seamless ticketing, point-of-sale, self-serve kiosks, memberships and digital waiver processes.</p> <p>But here's the best part: our team. title: Senior Data Scientist - Credit Risk Modelling
description: Senior Data Scientist - Credit Risk Modelling Hybrid in London or remote in the UK We’re looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join our Credit Risk Modelling team. You'll shape how iwoca models credit risk – setting the technical direction on multi-quarter projects, and lifting the bar for the team as you go. The company Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are. That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed. We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive. The team The Credit Risk Modelling team owns credit risk and Customer Lifetime Value (CLtV) modelling for iwoca's UK and German lending. That covers the probabilistic machine learning models behind every credit decision, plus the CLtV models that shape pricing and portfolio strategy. The team is around twelve data scientists. Some work on auto-space models that decide within five minutes from data candidates authorise us to pull. Others work on manual-space models that pick up when a credit analyst adds digital footprint and income data, which lands a decision within 24 hours. The role You'll own credit and CLtV modelling projects end to end, from spotting where the modelling stack is holding the business back through to landing the change. The work spans keeping production models healthy, incremental development, and research that reshapes how the models work. AI has lowered the cost of prototyping enough that ideas which used to sit below the priority line are now viable, so the R&D share of the role is growing. Live examples of the work: Causal estimation of offer terms. Modelling how amount, duration, and price shape customer outcomes. Unifying auto and manual models. The two families were built without forced technical alignment. Finding a principled way to unify them on a common cost function is open work. IFRS accounting model. A multi-stage credit model where information propagates back from later-stage recovery predictions to sharpen upfront loss estimates. Generalising credit and CLtV. Whether a more general framing could replace both separate models is an open research question. The requirements Essential: Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience. Statistical foundations. You have a background in probability and statistics from a quantitative field. You reason about uncertainty and calibration as first-order concerns. Production ML. You have built and shipped supervised ML models end to end – exploration, training, deployment, monitoring. Research mindset. You proactively explore new ways to add value. R&D time is when you expect to find the next step change. Judgement. You critically evaluate model output – yours, a colleague's, or an LLM's – and can explain why a choice is right. You defend your reasoning under challenge, and challenge others' when the evidence points elsewhere. You've influenced technical direction beyond your own projects. Project leadership. You've owned modelling projects end to end, from spotting the opportunity through framing, method choice, shipping, and landing the commercial impact. You move fast, iterate, and update on new evidence rather than chase perfection. AI fluency. You use AI as a primary tool. You prototype with it, automate with it, and take on R&D that would not otherwise be viable. You use judgement on where it helps and where it doesn't. Bonus: Domain experience. You have worked in credit risk, lending, or customer lifetime value modelling. Non-linear methods. You have shipped gradient boosting or neural networks on tabular data in production. Bayesian methods. You have used hierarchical models, MCMC, or Bayesian updating in real work. Time series modelling. You have modelled temporal data where autocorrelation, drift, or seasonality mattered. Python. The stack the team uses. The salary We expect to pay from £90,000 – £120,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews. The culture At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective. We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them. The offices We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work: Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks. Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions. The benefits Flexible working hours. Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership. A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents. 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave. A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years. Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support. 3% Pension contributions on total earnings. An employee equity incentive scheme. Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money. Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme. Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield. And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer: A learning and development budget for everyone. Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers. Access to learning platforms like Treehouse. Role Overview Harvey is looking for a Compensation Business Partner to ensure our compensation philosophy, principles, and practices extend to all of our markets outside of the US, initially focused on EMEA and APAC. This will be our first Compensation Business Partner dedicated to our international business sitting within the EMEA region, and an opportunity to help shape how Harvey approaches compensation as we continue to scale globally. You’ll partner closely with our People Business Partners, Recruiting team, business leaders, and the broader Compensation team to ensure our programs remain competitive, thoughtful, and scalable across markets. We’re looking for someone who combines deep compensation expertise with strong business judgment. You should be equally comfortable analyzing market data, advising a recruiter on a complex offer, partnering with a PBP and developing a point of view on how Harvey should approach compensation in a new or rapidly evolving market. Help evolve Harvey's international compensation strategy as we scale, including our approach to geographic differentiation, market positioning, salary structures, and equity. Bring deep equity expertise and help translate Harvey's equity philosophy across markets where candidate expectations and familiarity with US-style equity compensation can vary significantly. Research emerging compensation practices and talent trends, particularly across the rapidly evolving AI market, and turn external data into clear recommendations for Harvey. Conduct market analyses using compensation survey data and other sources, while applying judgment. Partner with the broader Compensation team on compensation cycles, benchmarking, band development, and company-wide programs, ensuring international considerations are represented from the beginning. Identify where our US practices translate internationally—and where they don't—and proactively recommend changes as Harvey enters and scales in new markets. Help build the infrastructure, principles, and enablement that will allow Harvey's international compensation approach to scale. What You Have 5-7+ years of experience in compensation Experience supporting international compensation across EMEA and/or APAC. Experience working for a US-headquartered company, with a strong understanding of how global compensation programs are designed and adapted for international markets. Meaningful experience with equity compensation, including the ability to explain and advise on equity in markets with different norms and expectations. Experience in a high-growth startup or scale-up environment; you are comfortable building while the company and market are changing around you. Strong knowledge of compensation fundamentals including market benchmarking, salary structures, job leveling, offers, promotions, retention, and pay decisions. Exceptional business partnership skills. You can build trust with leaders, PBPs, and recruiters while being willing to challenge assumptions. Strong analytical skills paired with excellent judgment—you know when the data is telling you something and when it requires additional context. Intellectual curiosity and a genuine appetite to become an expert on the AI talent market, including proactively researching competitors, compensation trends, and emerging practices. Comfortable operating with ambiguity and building new approaches rather than relying on an established playbook. description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>Company Description:</strong> Systemiq is a system-change company committed to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals and the Paris Agreement by transforming markets and business models across five key systems: nature and food, materials and circularity, energy, urban areas, and sustainable finance.</p> <p>As a certified B Corp, we combine strategic advisory with high-impact, on-the-ground work, partnering with business, finance, policymakers and civil society to deliver system change. With offices across Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas, we are dedicated exclusively to sustainability-focused work.</p> <p></p> <p> </p></div><p></p> <h2>Strategy Associate, Materials & Circular Economy</h2> <p><strong>Location: London preferred. Amsterdam also possible</strong></p> <p>Systemiq is looking for a Strategy Associate to join our Materials & Circular Economy team. This role is suited to someone who combines strong strategic thinking with the intellectual curiosity to tackle complex sustainability challenges.</p> <p>You will work on some of the most important questions facing companies, governments and wider society as they shift towards more circular and sustainable models. Projects can range from shaping corporate strategy and identifying new business opportunities to assessing value chains, developing policy recommendations and designing system-level interventions.</p> <p>We are looking for someone who can bring the core toolkit and pace of a strong strategy consultant: structured problem-solving, analytical rigour, clear communication and sound judgement. Strategy consulting experience is one route to demonstrating this. We are equally interested in candidates from other demanding analytical environments who can show the same quality of thinking and ability to turn complexity into clear recommendations.</p> <p>You will join small, senior-led project teams and take meaningful responsibility from the outset. You will structure problems, conduct analysis, develop insights and work directly with clients to translate those insights into practical strategic choices.</p> <h3>Responsibilities</h3> <p>You will:</p> <ul> <li> <p><strong>Structure complex problems:</strong> break ambiguous questions into clear workstreams, hypotheses and analytical priorities.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Generate insights:</strong> conduct rigorous qualitative and quantitative analysis, drawing conclusions from incomplete or complex information.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Shape recommendations:</strong> translate analysis into clear, concise and practical strategic recommendations.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Develop client materials:</strong> produce high-quality presentations, briefings and other client-ready outputs.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Engage with clients:</strong> work directly with senior stakeholders across businesses, governments, foundations and non-governmental organisations.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Contribute to project direction:</strong> help shape project approaches, hypotheses and emerging strategic conclusions.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Build trusted relationships:</strong> work effectively with clients, partners and stakeholders across multi-organisation initiatives.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>About the team</h3> <p>You will be part of Systemiq's Materials & Circular Economy platform, led by Partner Ben Dixon.</p> <p>Ben works across circular economy and energy topics and has advised organisations including the Ellen MacArthur Foundation, the United Nations International Resource Panel and multinational companies across packaging, chemicals and related sectors. He also leads Systemiq's work on plastics, focused on accelerating the transition towards a more circular and resource-efficient plastics system.</p> <h3>What we are looking for</h3> <h4>Strategy and analytical capability</h4> <p>We are looking for candidates who already demonstrate, or can quickly operate with, the core toolkit expected in strategy consulting. You should be able to:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Structure complex and ambiguous problems into clear components, hypotheses and analytical questions.</p> </li> <li> <p>Apply strong analytical judgement to qualitative and quantitative information.</p> </li> <li> <p>Synthesize complex material into concise insights and decision-relevant recommendations.</p> </li> <li> <p>Communicate clearly in writing and verbally, including through high-quality presentation materials.</p> </li> <li> <p>Work effectively at pace, managing changing priorities and imperfect information.</p> </li> <li> <p>Move comfortably between detailed analysis and the broader strategic question.</p> </li> </ul> <h4>Experience and background</h4> <p>You will typically bring:</p> <ul> <li> <p>At least two years of experience in strategy consulting, advisory or another analytically demanding environment.</p> </li> <li> <p>Evidence of strong performance and increasing responsibility in your previous roles.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience contributing to strategy, investment, commercial or other decision-focused work.</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong academic achievement, typically including a Master's degree or equivalent experience.</p> </li> </ul> <p>We particularly welcome candidates from strategy consulting, but relevant experience could also come from corporate strategy, investing, high-growth businesses, specialist advisory firms or other project-based environments where structured thinking and analytical rigour are central to the role.</p> <h4>Sector interest and understanding</h4> <p>You do not need to be a specialist across every part of the Materials & Circular Economy agenda. You should, however, bring:</p> <ul> <li> <p>An understanding of, or demonstrated ability to learn, complex industrial and consumer value chains.</p> </li> <li> <p>Exposure to sectors such as plastics, petrochemicals, chemicals, consumer goods, manufacturing, mobility, energy or waste management.</p> </li> <li> <p>A strong interest in sustainability, circular economy and the economic and strategic questions involved in system change.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>Location</h3> <p>London is the preferred location for this role. We would also consider Amsterdam for candidates whose experience and capabilities are an especially strong match for the position.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><div id="description__body"></div> <p><strong data-start="578" data-end="603">Diversity & Inclusion</strong><br data-start="603" data-end="606">At Systemiq, we absolutely believe diverse perspectives are essential to driving system change. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where people feel respected, supported and able to do their best work.</p> <p>Click <a href="https://www.systemiq.earth/privacy-policy/">here</a> to view our Data Policy.</p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Software Engineer - Triton
description: <h3 class="PDq2pG_selectionAnchorContainer" data-start="135" data-end="148">About the job</h3> <p data-start="150" data-end="229">Build the framework support that helps AI developers unlock Graphcore hardware.</p> <p data-start="231" data-end="458">You will help Graphcore accelerators work seamlessly with state-of-the-art ML frameworks, including Triton and PyTorch. Reporting to a Team Lead in Frameworks, you will design, implement, optimise and support critical software.</p> <p data-start="460" data-end="660">Your work will shape how researchers and engineers use Graphcore hardware for demanding machine learning workloads. You will improve performance, quality and usability across a complex software stack.</p> <p data-start="662" data-end="874">You will join our Triton team, delivering new features, reviewing code, writing technical documentation and working with upstream communities. You will also help coordinate open-ended technical work across teams.</p> <p data-start="876" data-end="1046">This role offers deep technical ownership and visible impact as the ML software landscape evolves. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you.</p> <h3 data-start="3650" data-end="3676">Join the Team at Graphcore</h3> <p data-start="3678" data-end="3957">Graphcore is one of the world’s leading innovators in Artificial Intelligence compute. It is developing hardware, software and systems infrastructure that will unlock the next generation of AI breakthroughs and power the widespread adoption of AI solutions across every industry.</p> <p data-start="3959" data-end="4241">As part of the SoftBank Group, Graphcore is a member of an elite family of companies responsible for some of the world’s most transformative technologies. Together, they share a bold vision: to enable Artificial Super Intelligence and ensure its benefits are accessible to everyone.</p> <p data-start="4243" data-end="4565">Graphcore’s teams are drawn from diverse backgrounds and bring a broad range of skills and perspectives. A melting pot of AI research specialists, silicon designers, software engineers and systems architects, Graphcore brings together deep expertise to solve complex problems and deliver meaningful progress in AI compute.</p> <p data-start="4567" data-end="4710" data-is-last-node="" data-is-only-node="">If you want to shape the frameworks developers use to push AI compute forward, we’d love to hear from you. Apply now to be part of the journey.</p> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Software Engineer
description: <h3><strong>Senior Engineer</strong></h3> <p>Location: Bristol, London or Edinburgh (hybrid, three days a week in the office)</p> <p>Level: Senior Engineer II (TL1)</p> <p>Team: Engineering</p> <p>Contract: Permanent</p> <p>Reporting To: Software Engineering Manager</p> <p> </p> <p><strong>About Kaluza</strong></p> <p>Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.</p> <p> </p> <p>Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.</p> <p> </p> <p>With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.</p> <p> </p> <p><strong>What you’ll do</strong></p> <p>You’ll join a technology community of product-focused and data-led product and platform engineers working at scale. We have a diverse ecosystem, spanning TypeScript on AWS, Go on GCP and Scala, we index on product-minded problem solving over language purity.</p> <p>As a Senior Engineer you’ll own a slice of the product end-to-end, from design through to production, and you’ll build AI coding agents as your default. We’re looking for someone whose judgement is worth more than their typing speed.</p> <p>From your first day you’ll have paid access to Claude Code, with a budget we don’t ration, and access to the systems you need through MCP. Our tools and conventions evolve quickly, and you’ll directly impact how we build from here.</p> <p> </p> <ul> <li><strong>Own a slice of the product end to end: </strong>shape the problem with product and design, build the interface and the services behind it, ship it, and run it in production.</li> <li><strong>Work across the stack over time</strong>: depending on the team you’ll work across the interface people use, the services behind it, and the APIs between them, in whatever stack your team runs.</li> <li><strong>Build with AI coding agents as your default</strong>: Break work down so agents can execute, direct them, and review their output as carefully as you’d review a colleague’s pull request. You’ll also maintain the tests and safeguards that let agent written code merge safely.</li> <li><strong>Stay close to the people who use what you build: </strong>directly or through our forward-deployed engineers: a supplier’s operations team, a customer plugging in a car at night. Instrument what you ship so you can see how it’s used, and turn what you learn into shipped changes.</li> <li><strong>Make good work the default: </strong>shape the codebase, conventions and automated checks so that agents and new teammates produce the right thing without anyone catching it in review.</li> <li><strong>Mentor the team around you:</strong> Coach and mentor your peers and help improve how we work and evolve as a team. </li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></p> <p> </p> <p>These are the practices and behaviours we see most in our top engineers and value deeply, but we don't expect everyone to tick every single box. If you're excited by the role and can see yourself thriving here, we’d love to hear from you.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Experience shipping production software:</strong> You have a depth of experience in either a front-end or back-end of a modern stack, and potentially an openness to stretch across both as you navigate our diverse ecosystem.</li> <li><strong>AI coding tools:</strong> You build with tools like Cursor or Claude Code, can walk us through work you’ve shipped this way and review AI output as rigorously as a colleague’s pull request.</li> <li><strong>Able to navigate a complex, high-stakes domain:</strong> You keep complex energy logic legible across microservices, knowing exactly when to use sync vs async to prevent cascading failures.</li> <li><strong>Cloud and operational ownership:</strong> You're comfortable deploying on major cloud platforms using shared tooling. You fully own your software in production, which includes participating in an out-of-hours on-call rota.</li> <li><strong>Strong product sense.</strong> You ask the “why” before building, and you can describe a time when user feedback or metrics changed what you shipped.</li> <li><strong>Clear written communication.</strong> You write specs, pull request descriptions and post-mortems with enough clarity and context that either a human teammate or an AI agent can immediately act on them.</li> <li><strong>A multiplier for your team:</strong> You mentor peers and proactively shape how the team works; introducing conventions, checks or shared context that makes everyone else’s output consistently better.</li> </ul> <p><strong>It would be great if you have</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience building tooling around coding agents, such as MCP servers, skills or CI checks</li> <li>Experience in energy, or another real-time or regulated field</li> </ul> <p><strong>Our Values</strong></p> <p>Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:</p> <p> </p> <ul> <li><strong>Play to win:</strong> Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.</li> <li><strong>Solve the real problem:</strong> Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.</li> <li><strong>Build trust every day:</strong> Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.</li> <li><strong>Own the outcome:</strong> Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.</li> <li><strong>Go further together: </strong>Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>Our Perks</strong></p> <p> </p> <ul> <li><strong>Time off and family:</strong> 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period</li> <li><strong>Health and security:</strong> Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests</li> <li><strong>Pay and flexibility:</strong> Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% of salary to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work</li> <li><strong>Growth and setup:</strong> Personal learning budget, home office budget</li> <li><strong>Climate:</strong> Access to Furthr, our climate action app</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>Come as you are</strong></p> <p> </p> <p>We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.</p> <p> </p> <p>This role requires an existing right to work in the UK. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.</p> <p> </p> <p>Find out more on our<a href="https://www.kaluza.com/careers/"> careers page</a> and<a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/kaluza/"> LinkedIn</a>. Our Applicant Data Protection Policy is<a href="https://www.kaluza.com/applicant-data-protection-notice/"> here</a>.</p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Talent Acquisition Coordinator
description: Let’s transform banking forever ClearBank is built on the belief that banking infrastructure shouldn’t slow down progress. Quite the opposite. Speed it up and that’s when you unlock potential. When you really start to innovate. That spirit and ‘can-do’ attitude is why our clients – from FinTech's and crypto platforms, to banks and credit unions – choose to use our API to power their banking infrastructure. But it’s our people who are the stars here. They power that innovation, push harder to break boundaries. They make coming to work (or working from home) fun. They’re the ones we trust to catapult our clients to success. Just as they trust us to build a business that’s always striding forward. What you can expect: As our Talent Acquisition Coordinator, you’ll play an important role in creating a seamless and welcoming experience for candidates and keeping our Talent Acquisition operations running smoothly. You’ll coordinate interviews, maintain accurate information in Ashby and support the production of regular Talent Acquisition reporting. You’ll also work with colleagues across Talent to support supplier administration and help organise our monthly induction for new joiners. This role is suited to someone who enjoys bringing structure to a busy environment, cares about getting the details right and wants every interaction with ClearBank to leave a positive impression. Your role includes: Complete the day-to-day administration of Ashby, maintaining accurate and complete candidate, vacancy and recruitment information to support reliable reporting and compliant hiring processes. Coordinate interviews across multiple time zones, managing candidate and interviewer communication and availability to create a timely, organised and professional experience. Welcome and support candidates attending interviews at the ClearBank office, particularly senior candidates, creating a positive and professional first impression. Monitor recruitment activity and data quality in Ashby, identifying missing, inaccurate or outdated information and working with recruiters to resolve issues promptly. Produce accurate weekly Talent Acquisition dashboards and insights, providing clear visibility of recruitment activity and data to the Talent Acquisition Lead. Support wider Talent operations, including supplier onboarding and offboarding for the Head of Talent and the organisation of monthly new-joiner induction with the Talent Development Manager. Identify opportunities to improve Talent Acquisition coordination and administration, suggesting practical ways to make processes simpler, clearer and more effective. What does success in this role look like: Ashby contains accurate, complete and dependable recruitment information that the Talent Acquisition team can confidently use for reporting and decision-making. Candidates experience organised, timely and thoughtful communication throughout interview coordination and when visiting the ClearBank office. Interviews are coordinated effectively across stakeholders and time zones, with scheduling problems identified and resolved promptly. Weekly Talent Acquisition dashboards are produced accurately and consistently, giving the Talent Acquisition Lead clear visibility of recruitment activity. Supplier administration and monthly induction coordination are organised and reliable, with the relevant stakeholders kept informed. What you’ll bring: To excel in this role, you’ll also need: Previous experience in a Talent Acquisition, recruitment coordination or similar role, with hands-on experience supporting interview scheduling, candidate administration and day-to-day recruitment processes. Strong organisational skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple interviews, activities and competing priorities. Excellent attention to detail, particularly when working with recruitment systems, schedules, reports and confidential information. Confidence communicating with candidates and colleagues at different levels of seniority. The ability to use digital systems effectively and learn new technology and processes quickly. A methodical approach to maintaining accurate records and identifying missing or inconsistent information. The ability to take ownership of assigned tasks, follow agreed processes and ask for support when needed. A little bit more about us! ClearBank is Where You Can belong: At ClearBank we think about Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DE&I) a lot. Not because we think we should. But because we know we should – how else can we build a happy workforce and be successful as a business. We’re committed to making sure our teams reflect society. And we put energy and effort into making this a place where everyone feels at home, where they’re given the trust and encouragement to do their very best work. Here are some of the things we’re most proud of: 42% of our senior management roles are held by women Our enhanced family leave policies Launching our partnership with Code First Girls Increasing awareness of neurodiversity in the workplace through our partnership with the Inclusive Group Our hiring process and what you can expect: Application: a member of our talent acquisition team will review your application against the key requirements for the role and let you know within two weeks whether you’re moving forward to the next stage; Screening: You’ll spend 30-45 minutes speaking to one of our recruiters learning more about the role and ClearBank, and we’ll get it know more about you, your experience and how your skills align with the role (this will be via phone or Teams video call). You can expect to hear back from us within seven days following this meeting (if things are taking longer than expected, we’ll let you know that too); First Interview: You’ll spend one hour with a member of our hiring team focusing on your skills, competencies and your ways of working at the same time we’ll give you time to ask more questions about the role, the team and learn more about the ClearBank culture. This will be via Teams. Second Interview: This will be a competency-based interview with one or more members of our team. Final Stage: You will have a final meeting with the Head of Department. This will be around 45-60 minutes. Offer: Congratulations! Get ready to transform banking forever! Our commitment to you as a candidate: We will always try our best to get back to you within seven days of your interview whether you’ve been successful or not and provide you with feedback. Sometimes things take a little longer, so we may not have a decision to share but we will get it touch to let you know we need a little more time. We’re unable to provide specific individual feedback at the application or screening stage but know that your application was reviewed and considered carefully. title: Partner Engagements Manager, Compliance Strategy
description: Company Description We’re Checkout.com . We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers. Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale. If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact. With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started. About the role The Partner Engagements Manager, Compliance Strategy will lead Checkout’s external-facing compliance strategy across banking, scheme and other strategic partner relationships. You will own the operating model and delivery of compliance-related partner engagements, including annual reviews, periodic due diligence, requests for information, licensing and scheme initiatives, and readiness for product or geographic expansion. You will ensure that Checkout presents a consistent, accurate and well-evidenced view of its compliance framework, while converting external expectations into practical improvements to our roadmap, controls, processes and operating model. The role combines strategic ownership, senior stakeholder management and hands-on delivery. You will lead complex engagements, advise Compliance leadership, build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, and develop the partner-engagement capability of the team, including managing and coaching Senior Analyst(s) as the structure is established. What you will do Own the Compliance Strategy partner-engagement portfolio, prioritising work across banking partners, schemes and other strategic external stakeholders. Establish and continuously improve the operating model for partner engagements, including governance, roles and responsibilities, service standards, evidence expectations, response libraries, escalation routes and management information. Lead annual KYC AML partner compliance reviews, partner onboarding or refreshes, complex RFIs and other material external engagements from planning through to closure. Act as a senior Compliance representative in partner meetings, with high level input around Checkout’s compliance framework, risk management approach, policies, controls, governance and improvement plans with clarity and confidence. Provide oversight and challenge to response packs, control narratives, policy summaries, presentations and supporting evidence, ensuring consistency, accuracy and appropriate ownership. Lead compliance support for scheme, product-launch and geographic-expansion initiatives, ensuring external partner obligations and readiness requirements are identified, tracked and addressed. Translate partner feedback, requests and emerging expectations into strategic recommendations, roadmap priorities, control enhancements and process improvements. Build strong working relationships across Compliance, Legal, Risk, Product, Operations, Commercial, Finance, Technology and regional teams to align delivery and resolve dependencies. Maintain clear governance over engagement risks, issues, decisions, action plans and remediation, escalating material matters to the Head of Compliance Strategy and relevant governance forums. Produce concise and decision-useful updates for Compliance leadership, senior management and governance committees, including themes, trends, risks, commitments and delivery status. Partner with relevant second-line teams to ensure external engagement activity is consistent with the Compliance framework, risk appetite, regulatory obligations and the responsibilities of the three lines of defence. Coach, develop and set clear expectations for Senior Analyst(s). Create and implement a high-quality, scalable and collaborative partner-engagement framework. Identify opportunities to use better data, tooling, workflow design and documentation to improve response quality, reduce duplication and increase the resilience of the Compliance operating model. Represent Compliance Strategy in cross-functional strategic initiatives and take on other priorities that support long-term capability maturation. What you will need to be successful Typically 3–5 years of experience in a similar role within compliance, regulatory compliance, risk, audit, legal or a related function in payments, fintech, banking or another regulated financial-services environment. Demonstrable experience leading external partner, banking, scheme, audit, regulatory or due-diligence engagements. Experience translating regulatory or partner expectations into practical requirements, delivery plans, governance and measurable improvements. Experience leading complex, cross-functional workstreams with multiple stakeholders, dependencies and deadlines. Experience coaching or managing people, setting priorities, giving feedback and creating clarity in a fast-moving environment. Strong understanding of the payments ecosystem and the compliance expectations relevant to banking partners, payment schemes and regulated financial institutions. Working knowledge of relevant compliance domains such as AML/CTF, sanctions, KYC/CDD/EDD, licensing, safeguarding, operational resilience, regulatory change or control assurance. Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to present complex issues, defend recommendations and influence senior stakeholders. Strong judgement and the confidence to challenge constructively, distinguish material from non-material issues and escalate appropriately. Strong organisational, analytical and project-management skills, with a track record of delivering high-quality outcomes under pressure. ICA, ACAMS or another relevant professional qualification is desirable. How you will work at Checkout Be The Owner: Set direction, create accountability and ensure commitments are delivered. Talk Straight: Give clear, evidence-led advice and communicate difficult messages respectfully and early. One Team: Build alignment across functions and regions, sharing context and bringing people with you. No Room for Approximation: Set a high bar for accuracy, evidence, consistency and regulatory defensibility. Athlete Mindset: Plan rigorously, raise the standard and keep improving the capability of the function. Better Every Day: Turn recurring engagement friction into scalable processes, tools and operating-model improvements. Pace Matters: Balance urgency with thoughtful risk judgement and disciplined execution. Fundamentally Positive: Lead with trust, humility and a practical, solution-oriented approach. What success looks like Partner engagement framework is clearly documented with detailed SLAs and communicated to all relevant stakeholders. Partner engagements are planned, governed and delivered consistently across the portfolio. Checkout is represented externally through clear, accurate, credible and coherent compliance narratives. Material risks, gaps and commitments are visible to the right stakeholders and managed through to resolution. Scheme, product and geographic-expansion initiatives receive timely and practical Compliance Strategy support. Partner feedback is converted into measurable improvements in processes, documentation, monitoring, tooling and capability. The Senior Analyst(s) and wider stakeholder network have clear priorities, effective ways of working and opportunities to grow. Compliance leadership has reliable management information to understand engagement themes, risks, capacity and progress. Additional Information Bring all of you to work We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one. Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands. We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here. It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable. Life at Checkout.com We understand that work is just one part of your life. Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection. Curious about what it’s like to be part of our team? Visit our Careers Page to learn more about our culture, open roles, and what drives us. title: Europe Strategy & Operations Director
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><span style="font-weight: 400;"><strong>About Faire</strong></span></p> <p>Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.</p> <p>We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.</p></div><p class="p1"><strong>About this role</strong></p> <p class="p1">We're looking for a strategic, analytical leader to drive growth and performance across our European and International business. In this role you'll personally own a high-impact portfolio of initiatives, doing the deep analytical work and driving execution yourself, while setting strategic direction and coaching a small team of individual contributors.</p> <p class="p1">You’ll connect the dots across product and go-to-market, using analytics, customer insights, and opportunity sizing to decide where we invest and how we execute. You’ll partner closely with Product, Operations, Revenue, and Data Science, and become a trusted advisor to senior leadership across the business.</p> <p class="p1">This is a player-coach role for someone who wants to shape strategy and also roll up their sleeves to deliver results. This role is based in London.</p> <p class="p1"><strong>What you’ll do</strong></p> <ul class="ul1"> <li class="li1">Drive OKR attainment for the International team, owning strategy and execution for our Europe Top 8 priorities</li> <li class="li1">Lead and develop a team of Strategy & Operations ICs through coaching, prioritization, and vision setting</li> <li class="li1">Personally own key initiatives in Europe: identify opportunities that move company metrics, align cross-functional teams, remove roadblocks, and lead execution end to end</li> <li class="li1">Prioritize GTM and Product initiatives based on impact, strategic importance, and complexity, and partner with Data Science to build and refine the models that support those decisions</li> <li class="li1">Proactively identify opportunities that grow retailer lifetime value (LTV)</li> <li class="li1">Drive forecasting, performance monitoring, and metric decomps, and surface the insights that matter most to leadership</li> <li class="li1">Build effective, scalable operational processes and close operational gaps</li> <li class="li1">Build trusted relationships with key stakeholders across Product, Operations, Revenue, and leadership</li> </ul> <p class="p1"><strong>Qualifications</strong></p> <ul class="ul1"> <li class="li1">8+ years of experience in consulting, finance (investment banking or private equity), or analytical business operations roles</li> <li class="li1">Experience managing and developing people</li> <li class="li1">Some experience partnering with GTM and Product teams</li> <li class="li1">You are an exceptional creative problem solver. You can break down ambiguous problems and structure a path to an answer.</li> <li class="li1">You are analytical and comfortable with data. You have strong analytical thinking and SQL knowledge, or the willingness to learn it quickly.</li> <li class="li1">You have strong product and business intuition. You can place insights in the context of broader business goals.</li> <li class="li1">You are a scrappy, resourceful executor. When something needs to get done, you remove roadblocks and find a way to make it happen.</li> <li class="li1">You are highly collaborative and influence effectively through others</li> <li class="li1">You are a clear, structured communicator, both written and verbal</li> <li class="li1">You have a strong work ethic and an ownership mindset, and you stay calm and perform under pressure and tight deadlines</li> <li class="li1">You embrace the adventure and do whatever it takes to ensure success</li> </ul> <p><strong>Salary Range</strong></p> <p>London: the pay range for this role is £141,000 to £193,500 per year. </p> <p>This role will also be eligible for equity and benefits. Actual base pay will be determined based on permissible factors such as transferable skills, work experience, market demands, and primary work location. The base pay range provided is subject to change and may be modified in the future.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><em><span style="font-weight: 400;"><em data-stringify-type="italic">Hybrid Faire employees currently go into the office 3 days per week on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and a third flex day of their choosing (Monday, Wednesday, or Friday).</em> Additionally, hybrid in-office roles will have the flexibility to work remotely up to 4 weeks per year. Specific Workplace and Information Technology positions may require onsite attendance 5 days per week as will be indicated in the job posting. <br></span></em></p> <p><strong>Why you’ll love working at Faire</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Move fast:</strong> You'll own meaningful problems that serve customers around the globe with the agency to move fast and see your results clearly.</li> <li><strong>Equipped to scale:</strong> We invest in what matters, including the latest enterprise AI tools, to help you work smarter and get more out of every day.</li> <li><strong>Best in class:</strong> Our team is full of sharp, kind, and generous colleagues who care about their craft and about helping you grow in yours.</li> <li><strong>Real rewards.</strong> Competitive pay, equity, and comprehensive benefits designed to support your life inside and outside of work.</li> <li><strong>Belonging:</strong> We're intentional about building an environment where every Faire employee has equal access to opportunities, growth, and success.</li> </ul> <p>Faire was founded in 2017 by a team of early product and engineering leads from Square. We’re backed by some of the top investors in retail and tech including: Y Combinator, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Forerunner Ventures, Khosla Ventures, Sequoia Capital, Founders Fund, and DST Global. We have headquarters in San Francisco and Kitchener-Waterloo, and a global employee presence across offices in Toronto, London, and New York. To learn more about Faire and our customers, you can read more on our <a href="https://blog.faire.com/">blog</a>.</p> <p></p> <p>Faire provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression.</p> <p>Faire is committed to providing access, equal opportunity and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. title: Senior Sales Executive (Perform by Marcus Evans)
description: Marcus Evans is a global leader in business intelligence, helping our clients grow by making connections, sharing knowledge, inspiring people, building relationships and creating new opportunities. Since 1983, we have brought decision-makers together through high-level summits, conferences, online platforms and performance programmes, working across all sectors and regions. Our overriding approach is one of collaboration, and our belief that “We’ll be our most successful when we work together.” We recognise excellence and actively develop top performers into future leaders. Our culture promotes teamwork, continuous learning and global career growth. About Perform Perform by Marcus Evans is our performance-improvement consultancy. We don’t sell off-the-shelf training. We start with a diagnosis of what is actually holding a team or an organisation back, prescribe the programme that fixes it, deliver bespoke learning pathways facilitated by vetted trainers/coaches, and then assess what changed. Clients get a written view of the gaps, the fix and the result. Job Summary We are hiring a Senior Sales Executives to sell Perform to senior leaders at large organisations: Heads of HR, L&D, Talent and Transformation, and the business executives who sponsor their programmes. You will own the sale from first conversation to signed contract, working with our Programme Scientist, who builds the diagnosis and prescription behind every proposal. This is a consultative sale with long cycles, several stakeholders and meaningful deal values. We are looking for someone who has done it before and wants to build a book of business from the start. This is an onsite role based in our London office. Key Responsibilities Generate and qualify your own pipeline through targeted outreach, networking, referrals and social selling to senior HR, L&D and business leaders Run structured discovery calls using our Initial Discovery Template, so the client’s real performance problem is clear before any proposal is written Work with the Programme Scientist to turn discovery into a bespoke diagnosis, prescription and quote, and present it to the client sponsor Position Perform as an expert advisor, qualify prospects rigorously, and manage intake so each quarter’s cohorts are full and the programme stays selective Negotiate pricing and terms within our pricing framework, and take contracts through to signature Keep every opportunity current in HubSpot CRM, from contact to lead to deal, so forecasting and reporting are accurate Stay with the client after signature through delivery and assessment, and use the findings to open expansion and renewal conversations Share what you learn from the market (objections, competitors, pricing pressure) with the leadership team so the offer keeps improving Qualifications Required: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in Behavioural Science or related fields. At least five years of B2B sales experience, including closing complex, high-value deals with multiple stakeholders Proven experience selling leadership development, learning and development, coaching, talent, HR consulting or other professional services to senior buyers A record of meeting or exceeding targets, with examples you can discuss Excellent written and spoken English, and the credibility to hold a conversation with a C-suite executive Comfort with discovery-led, consultative selling rather than product pitching Right to work in the UK Preferred: Experience selling to financial services, banking, technology or other regulated, multinational clients An existing network among HR and L&D decision-makers Experience working alongside subject-matter experts or consultants to build proposals HubSpot, LinkedIn Sales Navigator or comparable CRM and prospecting tools Additional languages Marcus Evans is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity, and all employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit and business need. #LI-Onsite Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Product Management Director – Soft FM & Estates (UK)
description: About SINGU At SINGU , we’re redefining how the world’s most ambitious real estate companies run their operations. Our mission is to become Europe’s leading platform for managing warehouse, logistics, retail, and multi-site commercial real estate portfolios — empowering our Clients to protect revenue, boost efficiency, and unlock new value across every aspect of their business. Our unified CAFM platform already powers the daily operations of over 250 million m² of real estate worldwide , supporting more than 500,000 professionals. Following our union with the UK’s Micad and Germany’s net-haus, we now help manage 100,000+ buildings across 35+ countries — and we’re just getting started. Backed by a leading growth equity investor, we’re scaling rapidly and partnering with global leaders such as Prologis, ECE, CTP, Hillwood, Logicor, GLP, and Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield. As we continue to grow through strategic acquisitions and bold innovation, we stay true to our core values: adaptability, collaboration, and client focus. If you’re ready to help build Europe’s leading platform for property operations — and make a tangible impact on how the real estate industry works — join SINGU and be part of this transformation. About the Role You'll own a significant slice of the SINGU product suite: space management and Soft FM services – cleaning standards, portering, and catering – used every day primarily across the UK healthcare market . Product-market fit is established and thousands of users depend on these products daily. What the portfolio needs now is strategic direction and taking them to their next level of growth. You'll do that through a team of four Product Managers who are domain experts in the products they run. This is a hands-on leadership role . You'll stay close to customer problems yourself, you'll raise the bar on how the team discovers and validates work, and you'll have real autonomy to decide what's worth building – and to prove it works. SINGU group grows both organically and through acquisition, and several of these products arrived with the companies that built them. You'll shape the strategy for bringing them into one coherent ecosystem and lead your team through that change. If you enjoy taking a set of good but separate products and making them add up to something bigger, that is the interesting part of this job. You'll partner closely with Sales, Engineering, and Product colleagues across the SINGU Group so your portfolio drives revenue and solves real problems across the European FM market. AI is a must-have lever in our industry rather than a talking point: you'll be applying it where it measurably improves how our customers run their estates. This is a remote position with periodic travel to London and Kraków – roughly every two to four weeks. Role Scope People Leadership & Team Development: Manage and develop the Product Managers within the product team. Own the full management lifecycle: hiring, onboarding, mentorship, feedback, coaching, performance evaluations, promotions, and exits . Foster a high-performing product culture based on customer empathy, data-driven decision-making, and outcome orientation. Manage staffing and focus areas across the suite, reallocating product resources where needed to balance discovery workload and meet strategic priorities. Lead the team through change – new ways of working, a shifting portfolio, and product consolidation – bringing people with you rather than around them. Product Discovery & Strategy: Define and maintain product roadmaps aligned with business objectives, customer needs, and market trends. Decide where to invest and where to hold : set a clear, defensible position on which initiatives scale and communicate it across the business. Build strong alignment with the Sales team to ensure product discovery and roadmap priorities actively unblock deals and support revenue growth. Identify and resolve ambiguities, dependencies, and competing priorities that impact discovery quality and speed. Product Management Best Practices & Standards: Promote modern product practices, including continuous discovery, outcome-based roadmapping, and hypothesis-driven development . Ensure product teams consistently validate assumptions through user research, experimentation, and data analysis . Drive improvements in requirements quality, stakeholder communication, prioritization frameworks, and release planning. Cooperate with the Chief Architect and Engineering Managers to ensure product decisions account for technical feasibility and platform constraints. Drive the adoption of AI-powered tools and analytics to improve product insights, customer understanding, and decision-making quality. Collaboration & Cross-Company Coordination: Coordinate with commercial and customer-facing teams to align product strategy with go-to-market plans and revenue goals for the portfolio. Represent the company at external events, conferences, and industry forums to share product insights, build the Group's profile, and stay connected to market trends. Maintain alignment, knowledge sharing, and team cohesion with colleagues across the Group. Experience & Requirements Must have's: 5+ years in product management , ideally with at least three of them in B2B SaaS . Strong B2C experience in FM, healthcare, or an adjacent domain is also worth a conversation. At least two years leading a team as a people manager – product managers ideally, but we are flexible on the setup; what matters is that you have owned a team, not that you are ready to start. Experience taking a team or a product area through real change: new ways of working, a restructure, or post-acquisition integration – and bringing the sceptics with you. Demonstrable experience applying AI within product development , using AI-powered tooling to accelerate discovery and delivery. Proven track record of leading product discovery across multiple methods and translating insights into validated roadmaps. Strong commercial awareness : able to partner with Sales and align product decisions with revenue and retention goals. Data fluency : comfortable defining metrics, querying product analytics, and using quantitative evidence to drive decisions. Excellent stakeholder communication : able to frame trade-offs and build alignment across technical and non-technical audiences. English at C1 or above , written and spoken, with the confidence to represent the product externally. Nice to Have's: Experience working in empowered product trios (or similar cross-functional squads) with engineering and design. Experience in healthcare (ideally the UK market, NHS) , public sector, or government-adjacent markets. Familiarity with platform or multi-product portfolio environments . Experience integrating acquired products into a single coherent platform. Polish or German alongside English . Not sure you tick every box? If you are strong on product leadership and craft but light on one of the requirements, we would still like to hear from you. Why Here Real ownership: you own a portfolio and the team that runs it. Strategy, discovery, and outcomes are yours, not a backlog handed down to you. Modern product culture: we work in trios, practice continuous discovery, and ship to learn. AI that makes sense: you'll apply AI to a platform customers already rely on, where it measurably improves how they run their estates – not bolted on for its own sake. A stable base for ambitious work: SINGU is profitable and growing , with consistently stable results. Growth: SINGU keeps growing through acquisition, so new areas to consolidate and lead keep appearing. International scope: five companies and around 250 people across Poland, the UK, and Germany, with a portfolio that spans markets rather than one office. If this role sounds like a good fit, we’d love to hear from you. Apply and help us build technology that supports critical operations every day.
